label: Higher at D2 after reaching S1, and at D1/GO after an unrewarded trial.
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 8. At D2 it tracks the state just shown: higher when S1 is reached (about +0.18 to +0.23), lower for S2. At D1, and more weakly at GO, it is higher after an unrewarded previous trial (no reward input) and lower after a rewarded one. These three observed-only terms capture most of the variance beyond timing. The free fit adds a small extra D1 bump when the unrewarded trial ended in S1, a negative D2 term for choosing a1 (beyond the state reached), and a slight positive D2 belief_lo slope. Belief adds little at D1/GO. No future variables used.

issues: Minor: in misses on the short form, GO after a rewarded S2 trial is under-predicted (a2 S2 r +0.065, a1 S2 r +0.062), and D2 after an a2 choice is over-predicted by about 0.04. These errors are small next to the activation std of 0.21. Adding (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) in place of the GO term did not help (test 0.779).

Minor: the worst-fit windows show r at D1 building up over runs of consecutive unrewarded trials (0.27 -> 0.33 -> 0.42 -> 0.43). A two-back term (tv('prev_reward', -1) == 0) did not improve the score (test 0.760 and 0.701 in the variants tried), so the label leaves out nothing that matters.

The claims check out on test. The D2 S1-vs-S2 effect is the largest residual (choice x state residuals: S1 about +0.12 to +0.14, S2 about -0.11 to -0.13). Unrewarded raises r at D1 more than at GO (fitted weights 0.154 vs 0.095). Dropping the GO term lowers test R^2 beyond timing to 0.659. Merging D1 and GO into one term gives 0.754. Belief terms add almost nothing (0.756 and 0.765).
